content.text:
Catalog search now ignores accents, so `garcia marquez` finds the books catalogued under García Márquez. All 61 tests pass: the 60 existing ones and one new one.

I made the change in `normaliseText` in `lib/helpers/text.js`. It now splits accented letters into a base letter plus a mark and drops the marks before lowercasing. `searchCatalog` uses it on the query and on each title and author, so the accent folding applies to both sides. It is the only caller, so nothing else changes.

The new test in `test/catalog.test.js` checks that these queries all find García Márquez's *Cien años de soledad*:
- `garcia marquez`
- `García Márquez`
- `anos soledad`
- `años`
- an accent typed as a separate combining character

Letters like `ø`, `ł` and `đ` aren't built from a base letter plus an accent mark, so they aren't folded. For example, `o` won't match `ø`. If your catalog has many Nordic or Polish names, I can add a small mapping for those.

It now splits accented letters into a base letter plus a mark and drops the marks before lowercasing. `searchCatalog` uses it on the query and on each title and author, so the accent folding applies to both sides. It is the only caller, so nothing else changes.

The new test in `test/catalog.test.js` checks that these queries all find García Márquez's *Cien años de soledad*:

Letters like `ø`, `ł` and `đ` aren't built from a base letter plus an accent mark, so they aren't folded. For example, `o` won't match `ø`. If your catalog has many Nordic or Polish names, I can add a small mapping for those.
